title: Whistle audio as a new possession-boundary signal
status: Primary-source research and a bounded experiment proposal; no possession gain measured. This research agent acquired no gated media, submitted no form, made no outreach/payment, installed no models and changed no old candidates/reports. A separate concurrent boundary agent is implementing an optional upstream-demo smoke; its outcome is separate from this research.

recommendation.decision: Prioritize a synchronized whistle-audio pilot. It adds a potentially useful observation of referee stoppages to geometry-only D inference, particularly when the ball is occluded. Treat it as a soft, state-dependent cue and test its contribution on external matches before claiming significant gains.
recommendation.fastest_immediate_code_check: Use the small public NaoDevils whistle demo with an off-the-shelf YAMNet Whistle score or NaoDevils' own pretrained WhistleNet. This can establish runnable audio preprocessing/inference without gated media. It cannot measure football stoppage recall or possession F1.
recommendation.fastest_meaningful_next_step: Obtain one rights-permitted external full match with an audible original stadium soundtrack and exact matching video/tracking, plus a separate development match. Verify the audio stream and synchronization first. Then annotate whistles separately from D/live boundaries and run tracking-only, audio-only boundary/D diagnostics, and fusion on identical frozen whole-match splits.
recommendation.current_blocker: No synchronized full-match audio/video was present in the initial searched data caches. A separate optional public whistle demo can test inference but supplies no possession labels or broadcast-to-tactical mapping. Existing tracking-only evaluation matches still cannot support meaningful whistle-fusion scores without matching audio and alignment.
recommendation.competition_rule: Do not hand-label whistles, boundaries, possession, corrections or time-specific rules on the provided Barcelona-Athletic organizer game. Do not use organizer public labels to tune audio or reopen closed diagnostics. External other-match manual labels are allowed subject to organizer access and documented provenance.

local_feasibility_audit.runtime_caveat: These package observations refer to the inspected system Python, not every possible separate virtual environment. An isolated optional audio environment avoids changing the current possession-model runtime.

repository_evidence.finding: The broadcast and tactical recordings have different frame counts and timelines; there is no mapping table. Broadcast cuts, replays and zooms require alignment to the 199,319-frame tactical target.
Previous restoration required only tactical ATD XML/TXT; source video was not needed.
Current D heads are player-only; existing folds hold out providers from D training only and all five evaluation matches are previously exposed development.
New hand labels are permitted on other games; none are permitted on the provided organizer game, including for validation. Required methods/data must be accessible to organizers.

local_feasibility_audit.snapshot_scope: Initial cache inventory before the separately delegated optional upstream-demo prototype; any subsequently downloaded demonstration waveform is not a synchronized football benchmark.

verified_rule_facts: IFAB requires whistles for starts, several referee stoppages and some controlled restarts, but not for clear outs/goals or most ordinary restarts.

Permission to restart can precede ball-in-play. For example, a kickoff becomes live on the kick and movement, not at the permission sound. The referee whistle can therefore locate a precursor rather than the desired D-to-live edge.
The ball can become dead by leaving the field without an audible whistle. An unobserved whistle is not evidence that play remains live.
modeling_consequences: Classify whistle event versus non-whistle first, then learn a separate context-dependent relationship to live-to-D, D-to-live and no state change. Do not toggle D/live at every detected whistle.

Represent multiple pulses as one burst for event detection while preserving count, duration and inter-pulse gaps as features. Double/triple patterns are not a reliable universal code for restart/stoppage type.

Referee attention/warning whistles during an existing stoppage, repeated permission, advantage followed by a delayed decision, spectator whistles, replayed whistle audio, commentary sibilance and other tonal sounds all require hard negatives or context.
Audio does not identify the team in control. It primarily targets D and boundaries; ordinary live H-to-A turnovers, including most short spells, still need tracking/visual evidence.

match_audio_sources.audio_availability: Verified at corpus level, not guaranteed per file or representation. The SoccerNet-Echoes paper extracted commentary from 1,100 half-videos and reported 56 without game audio and 14 with stadium audio but no commentary. Its released missing-commentary spreadsheet can help avoid silent games.
match_audio_sources.preferred_representation: Acquire one authorized full-half MKV from videos-HQ, videos-720p or videos-224p and inspect its actual audio streams. HQ includes video.ini timing metadata. Resolution names do not establish audio presence, codec quality or exact sound/video alignment.
match_audio_sources.not_audio_sources: Frames, features and image-only clip archives have no waveform. The current raw-data card describes clips-720p-10s archives as extracted images, so do not infer playable audio from the word 'clips'. Echoes itself releases ASR text/timestamps, not referee-whistle ground truth or an unrestricted waveform license.
match_audio_sources.access_and_license: SoccerNet raw media is personal/account-specific NDA-gated for research and non-commercial use. Audio has underlying broadcaster rights too. Verify organizer-access compatibility before making it a required competition dependency; no access request made here.

match_audio_sources.audio_availability: Unverified. The public v1.2 data card promises panoramic MP4s and synchronized annotations but does not promise an audible soundtrack. Source trimming code uses ffmpeg stream copy rather than explicitly removing audio; this can retain audio that exists, but proves neither original recording nor released-file audio presence.
match_audio_sources.action: Probe one authorized MP4 before choosing this as an audio benchmark. If silent, camera cropping cannot create genuine referee audio. A synthetic inserted whistle is augmentation with designed timing, not real validation.
match_audio_sources.additional_caveat: The v1.2 auxiliary ball trajectory is interpolated from annotated events. Do not use it as independent input when assessing whistle/event boundary gains.
match_audio_sources.license: Dataset card CC BY 4.0, conditions gate on Hugging Face. Verify any separately acquired audio rights.

match_audio_sources.audio_availability: No waveform in the tracking/event products already recommended or cached. Gradient/PFF's official offer describes tracking/events, not audio. SkillCorner open per-match products are tracking/events/phases. Sportec's paper says video is excluded for licensing reasons.
match_audio_sources.action: Obtain the exact matching rights-permitted audiovisual recording separately. A scoreboard clock or provider frame number alone does not establish audio alignment, and event timestamps must not be used as model input when they are also evaluation truth.

match_audio_sources.audio_availability: Controllable at acquisition. Retain original camera audio and/or a synchronized pitch-side microphone with a fixed wide tactical view and optional operated camera. Confirm sound is actually recorded; some tactical cameras export silent video.
match_audio_sources.action: Record an external fixture with permission for model training, evaluation and organizer access; preserve unedited media, presentation timestamps, device clocks and audio-channel identity. Keep whistle source positions/microphone distances for propagation-delay analysis if available.
match_audio_sources.benefit_and_limit: Potentially clearest shareability and annotation route; amateur soundscape and referee habits can differ from elite broadcast. Use a later genuine production broadcast as an additional domain check.

whistle_training_data.name: NaoDevils / TU Dortmund Whistle Detection Dataset
whistle_training_data.verified_contents: Official dataset metadata says recordings are from a NAO V6 robot, with labeled baseline NumPy spectra and test-bench WAVs. Some original data cannot be published. This is referee-instrument/robot-soccer research, not elite broadcast audio.
whistle_training_data.license_and_access: Public metadata API reports CC BY-SA 4.0 and all listed files unrestricted. Repository code is MIT. Dataset license and code license are separate.
whistle_training_data.practical_size: Public test WAVs are approximately 74 MB and 83 MB; training spectra approximately 2.23 GB and test spectra approximately 605 MB. The code repository has a much smaller demonstration WAV and a 1.52 MB pretrained H5 network, suitable for a first technical smoke check.
whistle_training_data.preprocessing: Follow the actual upstream annotation source rather than ambiguous dataset prose: scipy.io.wavfile.read preserves native samples; per-channel 1,024-sample Hamming windows with 512-sample hops; full FFT, first 513 bins, 20*log10(abs(FFT)); model input (n_windows,513,1). Source annotation uses probability >0.65. Do not use a log-mel frontend, normalize sample amplitudes silently, or change sample rate without a validated model-specific conversion.
whistle_training_data.use: Train or verify acoustic whistle recognition and test noise robustness; add real stadium/commentary/crowd negatives before football fusion. Keep recordings and whistle exemplars grouped across all derived windows.

whistle_training_data.name: GYdevy / Volleylitics whistle detection
whistle_training_data.verified_contents: Author-published Hugging Face card describes full indoor-volleyball audio WAVs at 22.05 kHz with whistle timestamps; repository size is approximately 3.29 GB. It distinguishes raw manual times from band-peak anchored versions.
whistle_training_data.license_and_access: Card labels the dataset MIT; no access gate displayed at inspection. Original recording provenance and any separate audio rights should be checked before relying on redistribution. No files downloaded here.
whistle_training_data.use: Sports-specific acoustic pretraining and hard negatives. Indoor reverberation, sport rules and recording mix differ from football. Do not treat band-anchored times as independently established football D/live boundaries.

whistle_training_data.name: AudioSet instrument Whistle versus human Whistling
whistle_training_data.verified_contents: Instrument Whistle is /m/0l156k; human lip Whistling is /m/01w250. Neither is a referee-only category. Standard labels cover presence in ten-second YouTube segments, not precise onset/offset or game-state semantics.
whistle_training_data.license_and_access: Official labels/features are CC BY 4.0 and ontology CC BY-SA 4.0. Raw media is referenced by YouTube ID and timestamps, not furnished as an unrestricted raw-audio archive. Media availability/rights vary; model reuse is faster than reconstructing the full dataset.
whistle_training_data.use: Pretrained embeddings and broad instrument-whistle cues. Add human whistling, crowd, cheering, hiss, speech, horns and other tonal negatives; do not equate the label with referee identity.

whistle_training_data.name: FSD50K
whistle_training_data.verified_contents: The official ground-truth archive was inspected in memory. Its vocabulary.csv has no class name containing 'whistl': neither Whistle nor Whistling is in the main 200-class benchmark vocabulary. Do not advertise FSD50K as a ready referee-whistle-positive dataset.
whistle_training_data.license_and_access: Dataset-as-a-whole CC BY, but individual clips have CC0, CC BY, CC BY-NC and Sampling+ licenses. The official page also asks commercial and machine-learning-competition users to contact authors; no contact made here.
whistle_training_data.use: Potential background/hard-negative clips after individual license review. Broader raw collection annotations may contain tiny classes, but whistle-positive contents were not verified there.

whistle_training_data.name: ESC-50
whistle_training_data.verified_contents: Official fifty-class list contains no whistle class. It offers negatives such as sirens, chirping birds, clapping, alarms and environmental noise, rather than sports whistle positives.
whistle_training_data.license_and_access: ESC-50 is CC BY-NC 3.0; the smaller ESC-10 subset has different CC BY terms. Dataset is public. Keep source recordings within the published folds to avoid fragments leaking across splits.
whistle_training_data.use: Optional general negatives; not a priority compared with actual football commentary/crowd audio.

whistle_training_data.name: Small individually licensed referee whistle examples

examples.description: Referee whistle in a gymnasium, 3.329 seconds, 48 kHz mono WAV
examples.access: Original download requires login; public source page verifies description/license. No login or download made.

examples.description: Referee whistle for a free kick at a Spanish second-division soccer match, 0.698 seconds, 48 kHz stereo AIFF
examples.access: Original download requires login; useful sports-domain exemplar but not a commercial default.

examples.description: End-of-match football referee whistle, 1.933 seconds, 44.1 kHz stereo WAV

whistle_training_data.use: Smoke checks and augmentation, never an independent football test. Group all copies, crops, pitch shifts and background mixes of each recording together; one sound mixed many times is still one positive source.

pretrained_detector_options.implementation: Official TensorFlow YAMNet waveform-to-scores model with 521 AudioSet classes. Select instrument Whistle by MID /m/0l156k (current class-map index 396), and retain human Whistling /m/01w250 (index 35) and crowd/speech outputs as auxiliary/confounder features. Resolve by MID/name from the versioned class map rather than hardcoding cross-model indices.
pretrained_detector_options.input_and_timing: 16 kHz mono floating waveform; default 0.96-second patches at 0.48-second hops. These scores are patch-level, not exact onset estimates. For precise edges, use a separately calibrated high-resolution acoustic onset refinement and preserve each patch's support/center offset.
pretrained_detector_options.adaptation: Freeze the backbone, fit one regularized referee-whistle head on its 1,024-dimensional embeddings using external sports positives and football hard negatives. Compare the frozen Whistle score first to establish a minimal baseline.
pretrained_detector_options.license_and_runtime: TensorFlow Models code is Apache-2.0. Pin the official model artifact and its distributed terms. Repository Keras implementation requires Keras 2/tf-keras and warns it is incompatible with default Keras 3; use an isolated environment or official SavedModel.
pretrained_detector_options.smoke_sample_caveat: The official speech_whistling2.wav sample tests human whistling, not referee-instrument discrimination or possession correctness. Prefer the NaoDevils demo as an additional instrument check.

pretrained_detector_options.implementation: Existing instrument-whistle H5 network plus exact preprocessing/annotation utilities from NaoDevils. This is a compact specialty comparator with a robot-microphone domain shift.
pretrained_detector_options.license: Repository MIT; TU Dortmund training dataset CC BY-SA 4.0 is a separate artifact. Preserve attribution and check the precise model/asset notices.
pretrained_detector_options.availability_checked: Public GitHub tree and source README verify both demo and pretrained network paths. No checkpoint or waveform downloaded by this research agent.

exact_reference_frontend.reader: scipy.io.wavfile.read; native samples, no added amplitude normalization in upstream annotation source
exact_reference_frontend.timestamp_convention: Preserve native WAV sample clock; record window support and center explicitly. Threshold is an annotation proposal default, not a calibrated football accuracy claim.

exact_demo_asset.separate_prototype_agent_observed_format: FLOAT WAV, four channels, 44.1 kHz; verify against downloaded hash in prototype receipt.
exact_demo_asset.semantics: README describes a short demonstration recording with one whistle; it has no independent football boundary truth.

pretrained_detector_options.implementation: PANNs AudioSet tagging and framewise sound-event detection models provide instrument-whistle scores/embeddings. The panns_inference wrapper exposes AudioTagging and SoundEventDetection; prefer framewise SED rather than a whole-file pooled tag for timing.
pretrained_detector_options.input_and_timing: Reference wrapper loads 32 kHz mono; follow the selected checkpoint's sample rate and frontend. Its 527-class map differs from YAMNet's 521-class map, so use MID matching rather than index 396.
pretrained_detector_options.adaptation: Frozen embeddings plus a small supervised head are feasible; compare only after the first audio pilot to avoid a broad model sweep on a tiny labeled match set.
pretrained_detector_options.license: Core audioset_tagging_cnn repository MIT. Verify the selected checkpoint and wrapper notices independently.

pretrained_detector_options.implementation: A small STFT detector using narrowband energy relative to local background, spectral peak persistence, duration and harmonic features gives an interpretable timing comparator. Do not assume a fixed universal whistle pitch; learn/calibrate a small frozen range on external development audio.
pretrained_detector_options.supporting_research: A 2025 soccer-whistle paper describes one-second overlapping windows, STFT/PSD features and classifiers, using 3.3-4.2 kHz prominence in its data. That supports feasibility, not a universal operating band or this project's performance.

alignment_and_audio_quality_protocol.probe_before_download_expansion: ffprobe the exact authorized file for audio codec, sample rate, channel count, stream start_time/time_base/duration and video presentation timestamps. Confirm waveform is nonempty/non-silent and contains real stadium sound. File extension and resolution are insufficient.
alignment_and_audio_quality_protocol.preserve_original: Retain the original multichannel waveform and timestamps. Create 16 kHz mono YAMNet and 32 kHz PANNs derivatives as needed, but store resampling ratio and audio/video zero-time offsets. Test channels separately if commentary dominates one mix or channel summation cancels content.
alignment_and_audio_quality_protocol.target_timeline: Audio in the same MKV normally shares a container timeline but may still have mux/codec offsets. Broadcast-to-tactical mapping needs algorithmic piecewise correspondence; a single constant offset cannot absorb edits, halftime trims or replay footage. Use source visual/clock correspondence and, when both feeds carry the same live audio, waveform correlation as independent checks.
alignment_and_audio_quality_protocol.do_not_align_using_test_targets: Estimate alignment from metadata or unsupervised audiovisual correspondence. Do not maximize boundary F1 against held-out D labels to pick offsets. On the organizer match, no human time annotations/corrections/constants tied to inspected moments are permitted.
alignment_and_audio_quality_protocol.drift: Check correspondence throughout each half and after discontinuities. Keep confidence intervals/residuals for piecewise offset/drift maps, and abstain from audio fusion where mapping confidence fails. A small rate mismatch accumulates over a half.
alignment_and_audio_quality_protocol.physical_and_editorial_latency: Whistle sound reaches microphones after propagation delay, and broadcasters may independently delay or mix audio. Crowd/commentator reactions lag play; replay video may have original replayed or continuing live audio. Distinguish mapping delay from acoustic propagation and permission-to-action delay.
alignment_and_audio_quality_protocol.noise_stress: Evaluate held-out real crowd whistles, cheering, commentary, hiss, horns, codec loss, clipping, distant/faint whistles, music and replay spans. Train-time mixes must not use evaluation backgrounds or whistle exemplars.
alignment_and_audio_quality_protocol.event_output: Store onset/offset support, confidence, instrument/human-whistle scores, burst grouping, channel, replay/live-context flag, source PTS, mapped tactical time and alignment confidence; do not output an unjustified frame-exact boundary from a one-second tagger.

bounded_external_experiment.status: Proposed; cannot execute meaningful match evaluation with the currently cached tracking-only assets.
fixed_questions: Can an off-the-shelf detector locate real referee whistles with acceptable false alarms on football audio?
What fraction of independently labeled live-to-D and D-to-live boundaries have an audible aligned whistle, and how far away is it?
Does adding those predicted signals improve official possession spell F1, especially under live ball occlusion, without creating false D intervals?
bounded_external_experiment.data_budget: Minimum feasibility: one external development match and one separate full confirmation match with synchronized audio/video/tracking. Prefer at least three production/source groups for a defensible source holdout. Before acquisition, freeze match IDs, intended-use terms, upstream exposure audit, split and model/checkpoint hashes. One held-out match remains limited confirmation, not broad generalization proof.
split_and_masks: Keep every crop/channel/noise mix from the same source recording/match in one split. Hold production/source/provider out from all learned heads, audio calibration, normalization and thresholds when claiming source holdout.

Freeze the existing tracking/H/A baseline and all native grading masks for the first audio ablation. Reuse identical eligible frames/matches for paired comparisons. Report whole-match and audio-available coverage; absence/silence is an explicit missing modality.

Keep full-match main results and an additional common audio-aligned subset. Do not drop cutaways, uncertain sound or difficult stoppages only from the fused arm. Preserve separate reason-coded unavailable/uncertain masks.

Do not reuse censored SkillCorner X edges as whistle timing truth. New independent boundary annotations are required for those moments. No organizer scoring or manual annotation is part of this experiment.

finite_arms.name: tracking_only
finite_arms.definition: Current frozen GRU/HGB ball-gap baseline with existing H/A attribution and decoder; same source audio may be present but is ignored.

finite_arms.name: audio_only_boundary_and_D
finite_arms.definition: Predict whistle events and D/live from audio alone with a small externally trained state model. Score event/D metrics independently. For an attributable official spell-F1 diagnostic only, combine this D stream with the identical frozen tracking H/A head; label the result 'audio D + fixed tracking teams', not fully audio-only possession.

finite_arms.name: tracking_plus_whistle
finite_arms.definition: Add a small set of aligned whistle score/burst/onset/time-since-event features and an audio-available mask to a regularized D/transition head. Keep H/A and decoder family fixed. Use state-aware transition probabilities rather than compulsory label switches.

finite_arms.name: tracking_plus_shuffled_audio_negative_control
finite_arms.definition: Use the identical fusion architecture with within-half displaced/mismatched whistle timings chosen independently of labels. This reveals gains caused by extra capacity or recording shortcuts rather than synchronized evidence; never tune its displacement using test results.

bounded_external_experiment.training_budget: One declared detector checkpoint (YAMNet) plus one declared DSP baseline for the initial pilot; a small fixed regularization/threshold grid fitted only to external training/development data, with three declared training seeds if a learned fusion head is used. WhistleNet/PANNs remain predeclared follow-ups, not additions selected after seeing confirmation.
metrics: Referee-whistle event precision/recall/F1 with one-to-one matching at 0.25, 0.5 and 1 second, false alarms per match-hour, and onset error; report spectators/replays as separate negative categories.

Audible-whistle coverage of true stoppage and restart boundaries separately, with direction/type counts and lag distribution. This is a diagnostic limit for whistle-only inference, not measured detector recall or model gain.
D/live boundary precision/recall/F1 and timing within 0.25/0.5/1/2 seconds on independently eligible boundaries, plus all-frame D precision/recall/F1 and coverage.

Official greedy one-to-one H/A spell F1 averaged over IoU 0.3/0.4/0.5/0.6/0.7 through experiments.metrics.evaluate_tracking; macro F1 for exact spell ties and the already predeclared 70/30 summary as auxiliary.

Short-spell recall/counts, conditional H/A accuracy, false extra possessions, per-source/match deltas, clean versus real occlusion subsets and audio-loss fallback. Bootstrap whole matches only when enough matches exist; overlapping audio patches are not independent samples.
bounded_external_experiment.decision_rule: Promote audio only after a paired official spell-F1 gain on frozen external confirmation under the repository's ranking policy, with acceptable D false positives and no material short-spell regression. A high whistle-tagging score or synthetic-demo success alone is insufficient. No numeric gain is predicted here.

on_external_matches_only: Whistle onset/offset interval, burst ID, audible/referee-likely versus spectator/uncertain/replay, channel and audibility confidence.

Separate independently judged live-to-D and D-to-live times or earliest/latest intervals, actual restart action, stoppage type, current team-control label and censoring/visibility metadata. Do not derive state truth by blindly copying whistle detections.
Video/audio source hash, period, source PTS, target sampling clock, resampling/mux offsets, piecewise alignment map and uncertainty.
Double annotation/adjudication of ambiguous whistles and rapid restarts; annotate silent boundaries as carefully as whistle-associated boundaries to measure the cue's real coverage.
additional_labels_needed.planning_estimate: For a ten-minute external pilot, approximately 1-3 person-hours of waveform/video annotation and synchronization checking is a planning estimate. Full-match independent D/H/A labeling remains approximately 16-34 person-hours from the companion data research; additional whistle annotation/adjudication may add several hours. Calibrate with the pilot; no work-rate study was measured here.

deliverable_limits: This research establishes accessible models/data and a concrete experiment, not a measured audio improvement.

No synchronized full-match audio/video is available from the initial cache audit. A subsequently downloaded upstream whistle demonstration can establish inference execution, but cannot provide an honest football possession-fusion score.

SoccerNet has audio at corpus level but per-file/per-branch presence must be probed; SoccerTrack soundtrack remains unverified; tracking providers do not themselves supply a waveform in the verified products.
Whistles are promising for selected stoppages and restart permission. They do not cover every boundary or solve ordinary H/A turnovers.
All historical reports, baseline manifests/candidates, source arrays and closed organizer checks remain unchanged.
